items.title: John "Picky" Brunious Interview, 1959-05-26
items.q: my brother-in-law was in there, Eddie Johnson... He played saxophone in the WPA band... he's the one that enticed me to come. He said, well, you ain't doing nothing nice. I said, why don't you come and play with the band?

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. Who was in the band then?

All right. Well, I'm going to tell you how to come to get in the band, you know? Yeah, go ahead. Well, at that time, they wasn't hiring anybody more in the WPA band because the WPA band was on their way, that is the whole WPA was on their way out because of what was it? Yeah. See? Okay. Because I'll never forget, in 1941, December 7, 1941, my wife and I were sitting on the end of the bed when they declared war. It was on a Sunday. Yeah, I remember that. It was straight. Well, I was still on a boat with Pichon.…
